title: FP8/INT8 quant variants: calibration & mixed-batch long-context throughput/latency benchmark
creator: Liang Chen
description: Objective: Produce a reproducible throughput and latency benchmark for FP8 and INT8 quantized builds of redwood-open-13B-v2 across mixed batching regimes and long-context sequences. We need to validate calibration workflows and quantify accuracy trade-offs so PM/TD can select default quant profiles for hosted API and Dedicated offerings. The outcomes must include: 1) recommended quant profiles for interactive vs high-throughput routes, 2) calibration recipe that limits accuracy regressions to <=1% average LM delta on our eval set, and 3) operational notes for long-context (>=4k, 16k) interactions and batching interactions (cold vs warm KV cache).
calibration_workflow: Calibration dataset: 1k diverse prompts sampled from customer-like workloads (summarization, code, chat, retrieval). Observers: per-channel min/max + 99.99 percentile clipping + KL divergence optimizer for activation histograms. Modes tested: per-layer symmetric AFFINE int8, per-channel asymmetric int8, and block-wise FP8 dynamic range. Steps: 1) run collect_activations.py (s3://redwood-calib/dumps/eng-10521/), 2) compute scales with calib_optimize.py --method kl --batches 512, 3) validate on validation split and save profile JSON to runtime/profiles/. We kept calibration scripts in GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-calib/pull/287 and documentation in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/ENG-10521+Calibration+Notes.
benchmark_summary: Environment: single A100-80GB (driver image rwinference/runtime-2.4), model redwood-open-13B-v2, sequence lengths tested: 4k and 16k tokens, batch sizes: 1,8,32. Key findings: FP8-balanced (block FP8) gives +20-30% tokens/sec vs FP16 for batch sizes 1 and 8 with p50 latency improvement ~18% and p99 improvement ~10%; INT8-thru (per-channel INT8 with KL calibration) gives +40-55% tokens/sec vs FP16 at batch sizes >=8 but exhibits higher p99 tails and memory pressure on 16k contexts. Representative numbers (median over 5 runs, cold start = fresh model load, warm = after 500 requests): - Seq=4k, Batch=1: FP16 throughput 11.2 kt/s, p50 95 ms, p99 420 ms; FP8 throughput 14.1 kt/s (+26%), p50 78 ms, p99 375 ms; INT8 throughput 16.4 kt/s (+46%), p50 68 ms, p99 540 ms. - Seq=4k, Batch=8: FP16 64 kt/s, p50 120 ms, p99 620 ms; FP8 82 kt/s (+28%), p50 98 ms, p99 560 ms; INT8 95 kt/s (+48%), p50 86 ms, p99 900 ms. - Seq=16k, Batch=8: FP16 18 kt/s, p50 420 ms, p99 2300 ms; FP8 21 kt/s (+17%), p50 370 ms, p99 2100 ms; INT8 24 kt/s (+33%) but observed OOMs in 1/5 runs at Batch=32 due to KV-cache growth and tensor layout increases. Accuracy: on our LM eval set (2.5k samples) FP8 average logprob delta vs FP16 = -0.25% (within noise), INT8 = -0.95% average, with worst-case slice (few-shot code generation) -1.7%. Calibration reduced INT8 regression from -2.3% to -0.95%. Observed trade-offs: INT8 is best for throughput-heavy, non-latency SLAs; FP8 gives the best balance for interactive endpoints with long-contexts. For long-context + large batch combos avoid INT8 unless using memory-optimized kernels or H100 80GB with kernel-level memory-savings enabled.
steps: Finalize reproducible benchmark script and add to CI (bench/eng-10521/run_all.sh)
Land calibration PR and publish runtime profiles to s3://redwood-profiles/eng-10521/
Update Console default profile dropdown with recommended 'fp8-balanced' and 'int8-thru' presets
Add automatic fallback policy: try INT8, on OOM/failure fallback to FP8, log occurrence to incident dashboard
Rerun on H100 and Dedicated instance shapes and record variance (followup ticket if delta > 10%)
comments: 2026-03-02 Liang Chen: Initial calibration pass completed. INT8 raw calibration showed large negative tail on code-gen slices; switched to KL-based percentile clipping (99.99) which reduced tail errors.
2026-03-04 Aisha Patel: Ran batch stress tests; observed OOMs for INT8 at 16k/32 batch on A100. Filed ENG-10521 follow-up to test memory-optimized kernels. See runtime PR link above.

2026-03-07 Marco Reyes (review): Please add p95 and p99 breakdown per request size and include cold vs warm KV-cache runs. Also add per-request token breakdown so CallCost can estimate per-request cost savings.

2026-03-09 Aisha Patel: Added cold/warm runs. Cold start shows additional ~10% latency penalty for FP8/INT8 due to kernel JIT and allocator behavior; recommend warm-cache warmers for interactive SLA-critical endpoints.

2026-03-11 Sophia Nguyen (PM): Recommend defaulting hosted interactive endpoints to 'fp8-balanced' and adding a knob in Console to opt into 'int8-thru' for bulk jobs. PM approved approach pending final numeric verification.
